images.text: Haven't you heard? Sao Paulo's Fashion Week has just wrapped. I was going to watch it from home but decided to join the captivating event. It's always thrilling to participate in the glamor and imagine ourselves just a little more beautiful! Wouldn't it be nice if we had such clothing ourselves?

What was supposed to be a convivial event, ended up creating a tense situation. It all began with the appalling news about a clothing line that was promoting the first evening. I know it's alarming, but the clothing store Holly's invests in child labor. A company that designs the wardrobes of wealthy middle-aged women relies on working children. Children who were supposed to be attending school or playing hide-and-seek. What? Doesn't the U.S. have laws about that? No folks, these children are in South East Asia. Isn't it convenient when regulations are different overseas? Aren't authorities in these countries aware of this practice? If you ask me, companies like this are supposed to use even more compassionate practices when dealing cross-culturally.

Like me, you may feel overwhelmed by such scenarios. But we aren't helpless, are we? No! We can start a petition at the website, TakeAStand.org. Shouldn't the organizers of the event do something about it? We can call and ask them to make a statement of apology for hosting Holly's. That's what they were supposed to do in the first place. Don't you think we should start boycotting stores that sell Holly's apparel? Post your reactions and get a dialogue going!

Negative questions have a different meaning than regular questions.
Wouldn't it be nice if we had such clothing ourselves?
Isn't it convenient when regulations are different overseas?
Shouldn't the organizers of the event do something about it?
Don't you think we should start boycotting stores that sell Holly's apparel?
You use negative questions to confirm information you already know, like Don't you think … ?
Negative questions can have two different meanings.
You can ask a negative question for confirmation of a positive belief. <b />You can ask a negative question for confirmation of a negative belief.
Be Supposed To and Be Going To in the Past Tense
You use the structures be supposed to and be going to when you want to talk about expectations, obligations or arrangements in the past.
I was going to watch it from home but decided to join the captivating event.
What was supposed to be a convivial event, ended up creating a tense situation.
A company that was supposed to dictate the wardrobes of wealthy middle-aged women relies on working children.
These children were supposed to be attending school or going to playing hide-and-seek.
That's what they were supposed to do in the first place.
You use be supposed to to talk about situations in the past that were expected and that may or may not have happened.
Example: It was supposed to be a convivial event.
You use be going to in the past to talk about something that was expected but did not happen.
Example: I was going to watch it from home but decided to join the captivating event.
NOTE: When you say be supposed to, you link the /d/ and /t/ sounds together, like this: be suppose_to
